description: A modular, stack-agnostic toolkit for AI coding agents to autonomously find, reproduce, and patch vulnerabilities.

written.description: Reads a codebase and its commit history, builds a threat model from them, and sends agents to chase each hypothesis it raises. It then tries to reproduce each finding in a sandbox and attacks its own patch to check the fix holds, working from source alone with no running target.

alive.last_commit_message:
fix(findings): enforce deterministic filepath validation and canonicalization

Addresses non-canonical 'workspace/<filename>' finding paths in knowledge.db
(https://github.com/google/mantis/issues/18):

- Deterministically strip synthetic '/workspace/...' and 'workspace/...'
  prefixes (unless '<target>/workspace/...' genuinely exists on disk) and
  reject Mantis virtual workspace artifacts ('workspace/findings/...',
  'workspace/kb/...', 'workspace/plan.json', 'mantis-summary.md',
  'workspace/repro_*') in report_findings and citation verification.
- Enforce a lexical single-file campaign filepath gate in report_findings
  (zero sibling filesystem probing / no existence oracle) that verifies
  line_numbers against the scanned file and normalizes every finding to its
  full scan-root-relative path.
- In directory and slice campaigns, repair 'workspace/<name>' and omitted
  leading directories (in both filepath and code_paths) when unambiguous,
  and deterministically reject ambiguous basename/suffix matches when 2+
  files in scope share the name.
- Strip synthetic workspace prefixes in canonical_filepath(), coerce numeric
  FindingSchema.id values cleanly, match string or integer finding IDs in
  write_findings() within run_id, and preserve existing canonical nested
  filepaths during ID-based updates.
